title: Cycle tenor and skill-velocity playbook: prescription for elastic commits and soft-trims
creator: Elena Kim
description: Purpose: Create a pragmatic, repeatable playbook that prescribes how we set cycle tenor, allocate skill-specific capacity, and execute soft scope trims (soft-trims) to protect high-impact work while maintaining velocity. Scope: guidance for PM/ENG leads for two cycle lengths (2w / 4w), step-by-step runbook for capacity modeling, soft-trim rules, surge activation criteria, and telemetry required to measure outcomes. Goal: reduce mid-cycle decommit churn by 40% and improve on-time delivery of engineering milestones by 20% across core platform initiatives.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook doc published in Confluence with step-by-step runbook and a 1-page TL;DR
Capacity model spreadsheet template with inputs for skill buckets and attrition modeled
Decision matrix for soft-trim vs hard-cut with example scenarios (low/medium/high risk)
Pilot run executed for Cycle 48 with two feature squads and retrospective notes captured
Telemetry wired: commit elasticity metric, skill-velocity score, and mid-cycle churn rate on dashboard
comments: 2026-02-12 Elena Kim: Created initial ticket and seeded outline. Proposed two tenors: 2-week and 4-week. Hypothesis: shorter tenor reduces merge contention but increases planning overhead.

2026-02-18 Jonah Mercer (ENG): Shared early capacity model with skill buckets: Core Runtime, Infra, DX, Console. Noted core runtime bookings have higher variance. Suggested adding 'surge cushion' of 10% for Kernel work.
2026-02-25 Aisha Patel (PM): Added acceptance criteria and prioritized pilot squads. Decided pilot will run with Runtime and Console squads to test cross-skill tradeoffs.

2026-02-28 Design review (Elena Kim, Priya Das): Discussed communication templates for stakeholders and customer-facing messaging for delayed features. Agreed on 'soft-trim' language to avoid premature hard cuts.

2026-03-03 Eng lead sync (Jonah Mercer): Implemented skill-velocity scoring: weekly throughput normalized by expected story points and ramp coefficient. Need 3-cycle historical data—blocked until we backfill metrics pipeline.

2026-03-05 Aisha Patel: Pilot kickoff scheduled. Action items: (1) instrument commit elasticity metric (ENG-2471), (2) finalize spreadsheet knobs, (3) run tabletop scenario on 2026-03-07. Updated ticket status to In Progress.
risks: Insufficient historical telemetry to calibrate skill-velocity—may cause over/under allocation
Cross-team dependencies (infra/runtime) could invalidate soft-trim rules if a single high-risk dependency emerges
Stakeholder resistance to new change window (tenor shift) without clear ROI communication
implementation_steps: 1) Finalize playbook doc and TL;DR for leadership
2) Ship capacity model template and run baseline for Cycle 48
3) Instrument two metrics: skill-velocity score and commit elasticity
4) Execute tabletop scenarios and record decisions
5) Run pilot with two squads; collect outcomes and retro
6) Iterate and publish v1.0 with handoff to Program Mgmt
notes: Unique elements of this playbook: introduces 'tenor' as a first-class variable (2w vs 4w), 'skill-velocity' to allocate capacity by domain-specific throughput, and 'soft-trim' rules that defer to canary/probe flags before hard scope cuts. Emphasizes telemetry-first approach and explicit surge activation conditions.
estimated_impact: Reduce mid-cycle decommit churn by ~40% and improve milestone delivery by ~20% (pilot target)
retrospective_plan: Collect pilot metrics, run cross-functional retro within 5 business days of pilot end, and update playbook with concrete knobs and example matrices for common scenarios. Publish learnings page and update 'CycleOps' handbook.
